Messages.Author: Jeroen
Messages.Body:
Hi,

Last weekend I've been talking to a number of people who regularly go
to tourneys and who are competitive players. A couple of general
remarks about the state of the game really came up regularly. I agree
with most of them, BTW.

1. For a deck to do well consistently NEEDS Auspex or Dominate.

Reason is obvious: these are the only 2 disciplines that have acces to
bounce. To make matters worse: dominate is already (one of?) the
strongest disciplines in the game.

Other forms of bleed defence:
* Rushing backwards against stealth bleeders is not always enough or
it'll probably just outright kill them and rushing a weenie bleeder is
often too slow to be effective.
* Intercept has trouble with 'blocking attempt fails'-cards. Besides,
when playing a deck that relies on permanents for the intercept you're
probably too slow to get you're defences up in time, because s&b decks
need pratically no set-up. And there's always Pentex Subversion...
* No blocking and jamming them on stealth? Most bleed decks pack
Dreams of the Sphinx, Visit, Barrens against this very tactic. AND you
need quite a lot of pool gain to keep using it.
* Bloating like crazy? well, this used to be a good form of bleed
defence but was seriously limited by the card changes in CE. 1 well
placed sudden reversal will still kill you BTW.
* Mastercard Defence: Major Boon, Archon, Protected Resources are IMO
not good enough or too dependent on the situation to deserve an Master
slot in a deck.

Other reasons why bounce is still superior:
* if almost everyone is playing them the above will not work and you
become the "horrible Black Void" for every bleed attempt.
* in terms of "number of cards needed for an effect" BOUNCE is not
only the most efficient but also the least card-intensive.¨

Why is there still no (inferior) bounce card for others?
disciplineless? Or maybe a master card? Or ,alternativly, more
vampires with dom/DOM or AUS as an out-of-clan discipline. And I mean
enough vampires for each clan.

2. Combat can win, but is less reliable than the other 2 deck types.

reasons for this:
* other combat decks.
* Big chance of killing your predator and getting a new one who still
has al his vampires and kan probaly kill you in one turn.
* Less 'ousting power' even with Fame and Tension. This means that you
CAN win a table, but sweeping is almost impossible. Not so for vote or
bleed decks.
* and, of course, the real killer, IMO: combat is too card-intensive.
Not only will you deck yourself really fast, but you don't have lots
of room for other things. The chance for handjam is bigger too,
because of the larger combo's you need.
* you're prey and predator will work together when you're a combat
deck by rescuing each other's minions. Something you cannot block. And
trying to burn minions will only increase the card-intensitivity (is
that a word?). Especially because you need to work around s:ce.
* 2 wellplaced obedience cards will jam you're hand with combat card
and no rush. The only card that counters that is Perfect Clarity and
it costs 2 blood AND keeps the obedience in your opponents hand. So
you need to play one every time.
* Almost no poolgain. In a combat deck you don't have enough card
slots for an efficient pool gain engine. Bounty is a step forward as
an idea, but should've been a bit better. Anathema is very difficult
to play with in a rush deck.

3. Delaying tactics

There's nothing realy wrong with this card. BUT once everyone is
packing 2-4 of them it really stops political decks from doing
anything. I've seen and played games like this. It really sucks to be
the vote deck. Related: people do have a reason to put this much DT
in a deck. Protect thine own comes to mind, and VP sniping with
Dramatic upheavel or Kindred Restructure.

4. Succubus Club again.

Nothing really against the card itself but 2 things about it really
bug me.
* the BIG one: slows the game down TREMENDOUSLY. A succubus club in
play alone should be reason enough to get an extra 30 minutes of game
time.
* threats of Power Self-Ousting. (Yes, kamel, this means you ;) )
the tactic of threatening the rest of the table into helping you get
VP's because you can self-oust by giving everything you have (pool,
minions and masters) to their prey. Kinda sucks to be on the
receiving end of that.

5 S&b is still the most powerfull archtype.

I know a lot of you are gonna say: "not over here". But it sure is
over here and on the most places I have played. That is most of
Western Europe, BTW. Vote decks seem to have lost their 'oomph' and I
can't figure out why. Yes, CE vamps with votes are bigger, but the
old Group 1&2 vamps are still around... Maybe because of the change
to 5th tradition? and, of course, see nr. 3 above. And the rise of
the number of DI in almost every deck?

This is getting waaay too long. Maybe I'll add some others points,
but these are the most important ones.

Comments welcome,
Jeroen Rombouts

Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
On 22 Sep 2003, Jeroen wrote:

> 1. For a deck to do well consistently NEEDS Auspex or Dominate.

That's the safe bet, but I'd dispute your heavily-emphasized use of the
word "needs". It is possible to take those 8 - 12 card slots and use them
to make some other aspect of your deck more reliable. This is purely
anecdotal, but I routinely play decks without bounce *or* pool gain, and I
do pretty well. Table management, timing, and good old dumb luck become
even more important without that cushion, but it doesn't matter if you
have 1 pool left or 100, as long as you get the win. But I do agree with
your general point that Dominate also having bounce is pretty crappy.

> Other forms of bleed defence:
> * Rushing backwards against stealth bleeders is not always enough or
> it'll probably just outright kill them and rushing a weenie bleeder is
> often too slow to be effective.

Outright killing them is OK as long as you get a more manageable
predator. Then again, I'm almost never playing for the sweep. Agreed
about rushing a weenie deck not being too effective, but that goes back to
what makes a rush deck good, and it getting ignored a lot.

> 2. Combat can win, but is less reliable than the other 2 deck types.

Agreed.

> * and, of course, the real killer, IMO: combat is too card-intensive.
> Not only will you deck yourself really fast, but you don't have lots
> of room for other things. The chance for handjam is bigger too,
> because of the larger combo's you need.

When designing combats, I try to keep the necessary components at three
cards or less. I spend a lot of time looking for two, or sometimes one,
card combat strategies; finding vampires with good specials, like Fatima,
Laz, Pascek, Thetmes etc. is very helpful in this respect. Even without
particular key vampires, a two-card combat is often no more intensive than
stealth bleed.... rush, card A, card B. Bleed, stealth, bleed modifier
(or more stealth, or perhaps anti-bounce tech).

> * you're prey and predator will work together when you're a combat
> deck by rescuing each other's minions.

Not entirely disagreeing with you here, but that kind of activity also
slows down the table, which is generally good for you.

> * 2 wellplaced obedience cards will jam you're hand with combat card
> and no rush. The only card that counters that is Perfect Clarity and
> it costs 2 blood AND keeps the obedience in your opponents hand. So
> you need to play one every time.

I think you could concoct equally frustrating scenarios for any strategy,
but sure, it sucks. Obedience is one of the reasons it's better to run
intercept combat than rush combat, but that's hard to win with in its own
way (although a friend of mine, Matt Guinn, keeps demonstrating his
ability to do it).

> * Almost no poolgain. In a combat deck you don't have enough card
> slots for an efficient pool gain engine. Bounty is a step forward as
> an idea, but should've been a bit better. Anathema is very difficult
> to play with in a rush deck.

This I really disagree with. Taste of Vitae has virtually no opportunity
cost if you're already playing significant combat, and provides the
foundation for Blood Dolls and Minion Taps. Provisions exists as well,
but it's a special case. The only bad thing about Taste-based bloat is
diminishing returns as the table empties itself of blood on minions.

> 5 S&b is still the most powerfull archtype.

> I know a lot of you are gonna say: "not over here". But it sure is
> over here and on the most places I have played. That is most of
> Western Europe, BTW.

My impression of Western Europe, gained solely from reading this NG, is
that there are indeed a *lot* of people content to keep playing Malk S+B
decks. Anything that predictable is ripe for exploitation, but I've also
been nuked fast and hard enough times myself to know it is frustrating.

> Vote decks seem to have lost their 'oomph' and I
> can't figure out why.

My off-the-cuff opinion is that a lot of people are distracted by the new
obf/OBF vampires and running PTO's because it's such an ego-stroke. As
vote decks swing back to mid-caps spiced with some key 7's and 8's and
just deal with getting about half their stuff blocked, I think you'll see
them return in force.

Vote decks scare me more, though. A (good) vote deck has an answer to
everything. Awful seating position? Move. Want to kill a weenie deck? Call
a couple votes. Don't like combat? Besides what disciplines give you for
defense, Banish, PTO, backoust, crosstable oust, bloat its prey, move it.
Anyway, sure it's trickier to get to the referendum, not have it Delayed, and
win it then it is to bleed at stealth or swarm bleed someone, but when you can
pass votes, your control ability is insane.

For example, early this year, I was morally opposed to being rushed by my
predator and had another vote deck across from me *and* there was no other deck
at the table that seemed to have any ousting ability, so I ousted my predator,
then my prey, then my predator to take it down to the two player for a 2-2-1
split. Couple of times in drafts ousted players crosstable which eventually
led to victory.

Combat decks have pretty strong control elements, though this is somewhat
dependent upon build, but they have ousting problems. Bleed decks often lack
control elements.

>This is getting waaay too long. Maybe I'll add some others points,

With it being storyline season, I'd like to mention something I don't think
gets nearly enough attention. While the evolution of competitive balance in
the game under WW's stewardship has been positive, there isn't a quick enough
rotation at the top. It's important to have significant variation over time as
to such things as the tier 1 clans and tier 1 decks. Even though weaker clans
have been getting better relative to stronger, to produce an interesting
environment requires seeing them overtake at least temporarily. May want to
avoid drastic turnover at the top, but you want constant turnover to keep the
game fresh.

It would seem a good way to do this is increase the power of
clan-specific cards for those clans which have inherent biases against
them regarding their discipline spreads or sect affiliation.

Take Assamites for example: Suppose Kali's Fang only cost 2 pool but
was usable only by Assamites. Suppose there were a Quietus specific
action put onto a vampire which afforded 1 pool gain every time a
minion were sent to torpor by the acting minion, or perhaps better yet
afforded an untap on a successful burn/torpor.

Anyway, there are plenty of examples where things could change among
the clans. It is a tricky situation for White Wolf to be in I would
imagine. They have an expansion design/release schedule they need to
meet. More importantly, each new set/expansion is structurally
intended for a relatively narrow set of clans--it would have been odd
to include a brand new Necromancy action in the Camarilla Edition.

Each set gives the various clans new vampires for experimentation, but
the strength of each clan is defined and determined more by what it
can do collectively with its clan- or discipline-specific cards. I
think this is part of the mass appeal of the Bloodlines Expansion:
There was indeed something for everyone! I'm not sure how WW would
accomplish this laudable goal with every new release, but it would
definitely help the game as a whole.

The problem with quick rotation of the relative strength of
clans/strategies is that players need to be current and up-to-date
with their card collections.

Sure, that's not necessarily a problem for WW.

However, I much prefer the way that it currently is, in that players
who haven't played or purchased cards for years can turn up to a game
and play competitively. Maybe they're occasionally baffled by some
odd disciplines or new terminology, but they still know how to play
and what is strong in the game. If the relative strengths of
strategies changed frequently, I think WW would make more money (at
least in the short-term) as players competed in an arms race, but the
game itself would suffer and there would be less incentive to play the
game for a long time.

You forgot a very important one - bleed reduction. There are several
cards for this. They're mostly reaction cards, but also include a
Master: Location. My Nos/!Nos Barons deck does very well with Banners
of Neutrality and Dummy Corp. The beautiful thing is that I also can
have an AI in my hand - burn the Dummy Corp and/or Banner if it's 3 or
less, burn the minion if it's more. I rarely have a huge problem with
stealth-bleed. (Plus that deck bloats like crazy.) I also love
playing the dom version of The Mole. That throws a big wrench in s+b
decks. They jam on stealth AND you don't actually get bled.

Yes, Telepathic Counter and The Mole still use the disciplines that
you are saying are overly necessary, but things like Ecstasy, Banner
of Neutrality and Dummy Corp are not. Bleed reduction, combined with
decent bloat, combat or forward motion can stop most s+b or
unblockable-bleed decks (and isn't vulnerable to Perfect Clarity).

Basically, one should assume that the default deck behind you is going
to be bleeding. Why? Because it's the only cardless way of ousting
your prey. That's the way the game is, and every deck should be built
to cope with it somehow.

> Why is there still no (inferior) bounce card for others?
> disciplineless? Or maybe a master card? Or ,alternativly, more
> vampires with dom/DOM or AUS as an out-of-clan discipline. And I mean
> enough vampires for each clan.

I'd prefer more ways of reducing the acting minion's stealth to 0 or
making an action outright fail. Not enough credit has been given to
The Mole and Car Bomb for their ability to do this.

> 3. Delaying tactics
>

> the vote deck. Related: people do have a reason to put this much DT

> Dramatic upheavel or Kindred Restructure.

I've rarely seen a situation where "everyone is packing 2-4 of them".
In a tournament environment you will probably see a vote deck or two,
but that much is just begging for hand-jam. People who play with that
kind of risk can reasonably expect to see some solid benefit. (In
this case, stopping the vote decks.) If someone has a DT at just the
right time, I say good for them. Nothing broken here.

> 5 S&b is still the most powerfull archtype.
>
> I know a lot of you are gonna say: "not over here". But it sure is
> over here and on the most places I have played. That is most of
> Western Europe, BTW. Vote decks seem to have lost their 'oomph' and I
> can't figure out why. Yes, CE vamps with votes are bigger, but the
> old Group 1&2 vamps are still around... Maybe because of the change
> to 5th tradition? and, of course, see nr. 3 above. And the rise of
> the number of DI in almost every deck?

I doubt that 5th has anything to do with vote decks losing their
oomph. Vote-and-bloat never needed 5th to fill up. That's what Voter
Cap is for. The change to 5th only hurt the "Prince Wall" decks,
which is fine, imho. I think the prevalence of intercept is causing
vote decks to show up less often. This is why my Ventrue/OBF
vote-and-bloat deck does so well, and why Lasombra vote can be quite
devastating.

The problem with claiming that "x is the most powerful archetype" is
that by saying so you ignore the multi-player aspect of the game.
Stealth-bleed, even stealth-bleed unmitigated by bounce, does not
necessarily sweep. Quite often it will tear up its prey and then
crash and burn against its grand-prey, who has had lots of time to
build up with no pressure from behind. But this is true of many decks
that go forward too strong and too soon. It's part of the game.

I've said it before, I'll say it again - Forward motion gets a VP,
table management wins the game.

So what's the most powerful archetype? The one that can manage the
table under any circumstances. But there is no deck-type with such an
ability. That ability comes from just one thing - the skill of the
player.

I think that happens because it is extremely easier to build a deck
this way with a collection of fewer cards than any other archetype.
Get one or two Malk pre-con decks, or one and a few cards with a
friend, and you're ready to go. With a Cam booster display (to get a
better crypt and a few more cards) you're probably up to reach the
finals of a tournament.

Alternatively, combat decks need a lot of different cards you won't
find easily in a pre-con, or won't find in good amounts. Compare the
Malks with Assamites, Brujah, Nossie or Gangrel ones: you get some
kind of combat-toolboxy approach, and won't be able to counter a few
dodges or S:CE. And the cards to circumvent this are often uncommon or
even rare, and anyone who owns them often use all they have in their
decks already and won't pass along. And we haven't talk yet of the
really good combat vamps, like Tariq, Pascek or the 6-cap !Nossies
with all-in-superior disciplines.

I've been buying cards since December 2002. I'd love to play a
tournament seriously with a Brujah or !Nossie deck, but how could I do
this with only one IG? Got one Gio pre-con, two Assamite, one Malk,
one Nossie, one Toreador, one Barons and tons of Cam, Final Nights and
Anarch boosters (up to the equivalent of two booster displays, I
think), and I own only one IG. So i'm stuck to the assamites (5
Psyche! cards is fine, I think) when I'm planning reliable combat,
and it took me months to get alternatives on them (more Fatimas,
Tariqs, Tegyrius, Clandestine Contracts instead of master Contracts,
more Market Squares for some intercept etc.). And I don't own yet the
necessary Freak Drives to try the Fatima-with-an-assault-rifle
multirush archetype.
It's not a surprise that I've made only one VP in 4 tournaments when
playing decks that not rely on votes, bloat or stealth-bleed. And made
my way to a final when I was not ashamed of trying the
tap-and-bleed-big Gio archetype.

You do want to make combat viable in tournaments? Make IG and other
anti-S:CE easier to draw on boosters. We don't need to be afraid to
make them common. we'll see more combat decks, and rushing your
predator won't be an issue since he's probably been rushed by *his*
predator. In all tournaments i've played, the problem is not relying
on Fame/Tension and rush actions to win; the problem is that archetype
is often represented by only one courageous soul in a five-player
table. Every table that happens to get two or more combat monsters
tend to be far more balanced, no matter if the other three are using
bounce, vote, bloat, S+B or whatever. And it would help a lot to get
new players, since occasional VTES tournament attendants that get used
to the S+B archetype are the ones who often become quickly bored with
the game - "is that all there is? i'll come back to pen-and-paper,
thanks..."
